transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2025-07-22
Start: 2025-07-22 11:00 PT
End: 2025-07-22 11:52 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Miguel Torres (Redwood Solutions Eng), Sam Wu (Redwood CSM); Jordan Lee (NovaHealth CTO), Rosa Martinez (NovaHealth SecOps), Ken Park (Compliance), Alicia Dunn (Platform Eng)
Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/security/audit-logs (security doc), https://redwood.example.com/samples/audit-schema.csv (sample export), retention spreadsheet: drive.google.com/link-to-retention-sheet

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
Redwood walked through what audit logs capture for hosted / dedicated / private deployments; discussed export options (S3, syslog, SIEM connectors), retention controls, legal hold, and encryption/KMS controls. Customer asked about admin activity (who changed model access, who rolled out model versions, API key rotation, token redaction) and where prompt data shows up in logs. Key ask: mapping of log fields to their SOC2/HIPAA artifact needs and sample exports for security team.

Topics: audit log schema, admin activity trails, export destinations, retention and legal-hold, encryption/KMS, RBAC/SSO integration for admin auditing

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate your time. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Jordan (NovaHealth): Jordan here. Rosa, Ken, Alicia too.
[00:15] Alex: Great. Quick agenda: we wanna go over what audit logs capture, how you can export them, retention controls and encryption, and then open Q&A. Priya will start on schema.
[00:28] Priya (Redwood SE): Awesome, yeah, I have a slide deck but I'll mostly talk through the live schema and a couple of examples. Note that my slides say "Sock two" in one place, sorry, auto-transcript, but we mean SOC 2.
[00:42] Priya: So at a high level we capture two broad categories: Administrative events and Data-plane events. Admin events are things like: user/role changes, SSO/SAML configuration changes, API key create/rotate/revoke, model version rollouts, policy changes, and console logins. Data-plane events are inference requests, embedding jobs, and the model responses we store for X time depending on deployment.
[01:10] Rosa: Quick question — does "model responses" include the full prompt text or is it just metadata? For HIPAA we need PHI never to be logged in any raw form.
[01:20] Priya: Good question. By default, hosted logs include metadata and a hashed prompt pointer, we do not store full prompt text unless you opt into request-logging for debugging. For Dedicated, you can choose to enable full request capture and route it to your VPC S3, but we also support prompt redaction where tokens matching configured patterns are masked. All of that is documented in the audit-log schema we shared.
[01:45] Ken: So for NovaHealth, out of the box we need zero PHI in your logs. Can you confirm defaults for hosted?
[01:52] Priya: Defaults for hosted: admin events = full; data-plane = metadata only (request_id, model_id, user_id if present, token_count, top-level latency metrics). No raw prompt text unless you've enabled verbose request-logging or set debug sampling. We also redact anything identified by PII detectors if enabled.
[02:20] Jordan: How do you detect PII? Is that on-prem or you do it in the control plane? Concern about sending PHI to Redwood for detection.
[02:30] Priya: For hosted we run detection in our control plane; however for Dedicated/Private we provide an on-instance detector that runs inside your VPC and never leaves the network. We can share the detection agent code summary; for regulated customers most go Dedicated or Private.
[02:50] Miguel (Redwood): And just to add — for Dedicated you can opt to have the raw requests exported directly to a customer S3 bucket with server-side encryption using customer-managed KMS keys, so Redwood never has access to plaintext in the export bucket.
[03:12] Alex: Let's walk the schema. Priya?
[03:15] Priya: Sure. Key fields you'll see: timestamp, event_type (admin|data), actor (principal id/email), actor_role, action (create_key, revoke_key, model.rollout, user.login), target (resource id), outcome (success|failure), request_id, region, model_version, latency_ms, token_count, storage_pointer, export_destination, k8s_pod (sometimes), and raw_request_hash.
[03:50] Rosa: "raw_request_hash" is that reversible?
[03:55] Priya: No, it's SHA-256 of the request body; not reversible. It's intended for correlation between logs and debug traces if you have a retained sample.
[04:10] Alicia (Platform Eng): What's in "actor_role" — is that derived from RBAC or from identity provider?
[04:18] Priya: We map actor_role from either the Redwood RBAC layer or from SAML attributes if you push mapped roles via SAML/SCIM. So if you have SSO set up and we ingest attributes like 'title' or 'groups' we normalize to our role table and include role_id in the audit event.
[04:40] Ken: Do you produce a separate audit for console UI actions vs API calls? Some vendors conflate them and it's hard to show exactly who clicked what.
[04:50] Priya: We produce distinct events for UI interactions (ui.login, ui.policy_edit) and API calls (api.call.infer). We also include origin fields (user_agent, source_ip, session_id) though for hosted customers we truncate source_ip to the /24 by default — you can opt into full IPs for dedicated/private with contractual controls.
[05:20] Jordan: Export options? We run Splunk and want to ingest in near real-time.
[05:30] Miguel: We support three main export modes: push to customer S3 (batch/near-real-time), syslog/CEF to a customer SIEM (tcp/udp), and a native SIEM connector for Splunk/Datadog that uses secure streaming. Splunk can be hooked via HTTP Event Collector; we can also send syslog to your collector.
[05:55] Rosa: For the syslog path do you preserve structured fields or is it flattened text?
[06:02] Priya: We send structured JSON payloads over syslog when the SIEM supports it; otherwise we provide a CEF mapping. The sample CSV we provided in the link maps all fields to columns you can import.
[06:20] Alex: Also note for Dedicated we have a forwarder that runs in your VPC and can stream to your SIEM with local buffering — helpful during network blips.
[06:30] [short cross-talk] Speaker 6: yeah that buffering is good
[06:35] Ken: Retention policies — what are defaults and how can we change them? We need 7 years for some audit trails for compliance.
[06:45] Priya: Defaults for hosted: admin logs retained 1 year online, 3 years archived (cold storage) by request; data-plane metadata 90 days online by default. We do offer extended retention as an add-on — you can pay to keep logs online longer or we can archive to customer S3 with your lifecycle. For Dedicated and Private you control retention fully in your environment.
[07:15] Jordan: 7 years seems long; how do we handle legal-hold or re-creation of the state for e-discovery?
[07:25] Miguel: We support legal-hold flags at the event-level. When a hold is applied we prevent lifecycle deletion for that record until the hold is released. For hosted customers we can put holds on exported archives; for Dedicated/Private you can set retention/lifecycle rules in your bucket. We can deliver an export in a forensic format on request.
[07:48] Rosa: Encryption at rest — are logs encrypted with customer KMS?
[07:53] Priya: Hosted default: server-side encryption with Redwood-managed keys. We provide customer-managed keys (CMK) for hosted upon enterprise contract; Dedicated/Private supports CMKs by default and HSM integrations for higher assurance.
[08:10] Ken: Do you support envelope encryption or bring-your-own-key with automatic rotation?
[08:16] Priya: Yes, envelope encryption pattern supported. You can bring your own KMS in AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or Azure Key Vault; we support rotation policies and we log key-usage events as part of admin events.
[08:35] Jordan: Audit trail for admin actions — do you capture the pre/post state of config when someone edits a policy?
[08:45] Priya: We capture a delta payload for policy edits with before/after snapshots for critical resources. By default, we keep the delta in the admin event; for very large blobs we store a pointer to the snapshot in export storage.
[09:05] Alex: Example: model rollout. Priya, can you narrate what we'd see if someone promoted model v1.2 -> v1.3?
[09:12] Priya: Sure. You'd see an event: timestamp, actor, action=model.rollout, target=model_id, from_version=1.2, to_version=1.3, rollout_strategy=canary/gradual, percentage, rollout_id, outcome=success. If rollout triggered an automatic fallback we log that as a separate event with correlation_id to the rollout event.
[09:40] Rosa: Do you log who approved the rollout?
[09:43] Priya: If you use the approval workflow in our Console, approval events are recorded with approver_id and approval_comment. If approvals happen out-of-band we can accept a signed webhook to attach approval metadata to the rollout event.
[09:58] Alicia: A few of our teams want immutable logs for a subset of events. Can you write-protect them?
[10:05] Miguel: For hosted, we provide an append-only export to a customer-controlled S3 with bucket-level write-once/read-many (WORM) policies as part of the enterprise offering. For Dedicated/Private, you can enforce immutability using your storage controls.
[10:24] Ken: Are logs tamper-evident? Is there an integrity verification mechanism?
[10:30] Priya: We support chain-hash integrity: each exported batch has a checksum chain that you can validate. We also sign batches using a Redwood signing key; with CMKs we can sign with keys provisioned by customers.
[10:48] Jordan: How are admin activities tied back to SSO identities? We use Okta; want to ensure deprovisioned users' events still trail properly.
[10:58] Priya: We integrate with SAML/SCIM. We keep actor_id as the unique subject identifier from your IdP, and we log SCIM lifecycle events (user.deprovision) with timing. If a user is deprovisioned, events prior to deprovision stay intact; new auth flows will fail. We also capture session_id so you can tie actions to a session even when the user record changes.
[11:22] Rosa: For attribution, do you capture IP address and device fingerprint?
[11:27] Priya: We capture user_agent, source_ip (truncated by default for hosted), and session_id. Device fingerprinting is not currently part of the audit event standard — we can add a custom attribute if you run a forwarder and inject it.
[11:45] Alex: OK let's talk about alerting off of admin events — can Redwood push critical admin alerts to Slack or PagerDuty?
[11:53] Miguel: Yes, there's a rules engine. You can create alert rules that watch for event patterns (e.g., policy.change by non-admin, mass key rotations) and route them to webhook, Slack, PagerDuty, or SIEM. Alerts include links to the event and context.
[12:10] Ken: Do alert payloads contain sensitive data? We need minimal context in notifications for security reasons.
[12:17] Priya: Payloads by default contain event id, actor, action, and a short summary. You can configure the verbosity of notifications; also we can mask certain fields in transit if required.
[12:30] Jordan: For our compliance audit we need a CSV export with specific columns: timestamp, event_type, actor_email, action, target, outcome, request_id, region, model_version. Can you produce that?
[12:40] Priya: Yup. That's what the sample CSV demonstrates. We'll tailor column ordering and field names to your auditor's expectations.
[12:50] Rosa: A couple edge questions — do you log inference latencies broken down by each token or just aggregate?
[12:58] Priya: We store aggregate metrics (total latency, decode_time_ms, attention_kernel_ms) in the logs. Per-token timings are available in debug traces but those are considered high-volume and live only for a short time; you can export them to your storage for deeper analysis if needed.
[13:20] Alex: Question about retention for exported logs — if we export to S3 and then you apply lifecycle, who controls deletion in that case?
[13:30] Miguel: If the bucket is customer-owned (recommended) you control lifecycle. If Redwood hosts the archive for you we manage lifecycle per the contract. We generally recommend customer-owned buckets for compliance.
[13:45] Ken: Are exports idempotent? If we request the same archive twice do we get deduped artifacts?
[13:52] Priya: Exports are idempotent — we include export_id and a manifest. If you re-run an export, the manifest will indicate already-exported files.
[14:05] Jordan: What about cross-region copies for residency and disaster recovery?
[14:12] Miguel: We support cross-region replication for exported artifacts; for hosted we can replicate to a customer bucket in a specific region under contract; for Dedicated/Private it's your replication settings.
[14:25] Rosa: Does the audit log include model input/outputs in a way that would break data residency? For example, EU data must not leave EU.
[14:35] Priya: For EU customers we can enforce region-restricted storage and processing. Hosted models can be pinned to EU regions; logs for EU workloads can be stored in EU-only buckets. If you use global routing we recommend Dedicated with VPC egress controls to ensure no cross-border copies.
[14:58] Alex: Let's surface some common pitfalls — Priya?
[15:02] Priya: Common issues we see: 1) customers assume default logs include prompt text; 2) forgetting to route logs to customer-owned storage for long retention; 3) mismatch of role mapping from IdP leading to attribution gaps. We include guidance in the onboarding checklist to avoid these.
[15:25] Jordan: About the ID mapping — our IdP sends groups as a single claim that is a comma list. Will that map to multiple roles?
[15:33] Priya: We can parse group lists and map to multiple internal roles; we also support SCIM provisioning which is more robust for role sync.
[15:40] Ken: Request for artifact: we need a formal statement in writing about what fields are never stored for hosted default so our security authority can sign off.
[15:48] Alex: We can provide a formal "Hosted default logging behaviors" one-pager and include it in the security pack. I'll own that.
[15:56] Alex: Miguel — could you walk the team through a quick demo of the export wizard?
[16:02] Miguel: Sure, I'll screenshare — just a sec.
[16:10] [screen share noise; Miguel narrating wizard steps]
[16:20] Miguel: This is the export wizard; pick timeframe, filter by event_type, choose CSV or JSON Lines, select export destination. If you pick syslog we provide a TLS endpoint and certs. We also show a manifest with checksum.
[16:40] Jordan: Can we schedule recurring exports?
[16:45] Miguel: Yes daily, hourly, weekly cadence supported. You can also do streaming for near-real-time ingestion.
[16:55] Rosa: How do you handle schema changes? If Redwood adds a new field will the CSV shift columns?
[17:03] Priya: We version the schema. Each export includes schema_version in the manifest. We support backward-compatible columns and we provide a transformation layer to map new fields to legacy column names if you need.
[17:20] Alicia: We noticed some vendors leak environment variables in logs. Do you scrub env vars?
[17:27] Priya: We do scrub common secrets in request bodies and environment telemetry. For Dedicated/Private you control what the forwarder collects; we recommend a deny-list approach for env var collection.
[17:40] Ken: Is there a minimum retention period if we sign the enterprise add-on?
[17:46] Alex: No hard minimum, it's contractual — we can commit to 7 years on-host archives under an enterprise SOC contract.
[17:55] Jordan: Can you produce an attestable export for auditors with chain-of-custody?
[18:01] Miguel: Yes we can provide an audited manifest with chain-hash and signing, plus a certificate of export.
[18:10] Rosa: A question about API key rotation — if an API key is rotated do you link events from old key to new key for audit?
[18:18] Priya: We record key.rotate events with previous_key_id and new_key_id; we also keep a mapping table for a configurable window so you can trace actions performed by either key under the same principal.
[18:33] Alex: Ok let's cover some nitty-gritty: do you store the admin's raw SSH username or the IdP subject?
[18:40] Priya: We store the IdP subject as the canonical actor. If you use local accounts we store the account username but encourage SSO to maintain central control.
[18:52] Ken: For offline audits, can you produce a timeline of all admin actions sorted with contextual snapshots?
[18:59] Miguel: Yes, we can build a timeline export that stitches events, deltas, and snapshots into a single forensic bundle. That is usually delivered as a signed tarball with manifests.
[19:12] Jordan: Is there a retention cost model for keeping raw debug traces (per-token data)?
[19:20] Priya: Yes, per-token traces are high-volume and priced separately. Typically customers export those to their own buckets and run lifecycle rules there.
[19:30] Rosa: Any SLA for log delivery to SIEM? We need within 2 minutes for certain alerts.
[19:36] Miguel: For streaming connectors we target sub-60s delivery under normal conditions; we can bake tighter SLAs for Dedicated/Private with local agents and network guarantees.
[19:48] Ken: Do you have a published SOC 2 control mapping that references these audit events?
[19:54] Alex: Yes, that's in our security pack — we map event types to SOC 2 CC6.x and ISO controls. We'll include that mapping.
[20:05] Jordan: A few questions from our compliance team that joined late — what data residency guarantees do you provide for logs associated with EU tenants?
[20:14] Priya: We can ensure that logs for EU-located models are stored in EU-only buckets and never leave region. For hosted customers that want firm guarantees, we typically recommend Dedicated in an EU region.
[20:28] Rosa: Does Redwood maintain an internal admin audit for customer-facing actions? Meaning, if a Redwood operator does something in a customer environment for support, is that captured in your audit logs?
[20:38] Alex: Yes, operator actions we take that touch customer data are logged in internal operator logs and those are subject to our SOC 2 internal controls; for Dedicated/Private we can configure an approver workflow and produce operator-action exports if you want that surfaced to you.
[20:55] Ken: Could you point us at a sample legal-hold workflow?
[21:00] Alex: We'll attach the PDF in the follow-up; high level: create hold -> target events by filters -> prevents lifecycle deletion -> audit who applied the hold -> release hold with justification.
[21:12] Jordan: We also need to know retention differences between human-readable console audit vs API-level audit — sometimes console lumps multiple actions into one UI change.
[21:23] Priya: Good callout — UI actions may batch operations. We record both the UI high-level action and the individual sub-actions as separate lower-level events so auditors can reconcile.
[21:38] Rosa: Can we get sample Splunk queries?
[21:42] Miguel: Yes we'll share a repo of Splunk/SIEM query templates for common audits.
[21:50] Alex: I'm going to note a couple items: deliver hosted-default statement, audit-schema CSV, Splunk/SIEM query templates, demo recording, and pricing for extended retention.
[21:59] [noise; short pause]
[22:05] Jordan: One operational question — when someone rotates a model with a canary rollout that fails, is the failed rollout event immediately marked and do you alert?
[22:15] Priya: Yes, the rollback/failure event is emitted and, if you have a rule, we can fire an alert automatically.
[22:25] Ken: For our internal auditors we may want a signed statement that Redwood cannot access customer-owned S3 exports if CMK enforced. Can you sign that?
[22:35] Alex: We'll work with legal to provide a statement for your contract addendum. We'll flag it as a deliverable.
[22:44] Rosa: A smaller ask — can you include a sample event showing a user.login failed with MFA challenge?
[22:52] Priya: Yes, sample events include mfa.challenge and mfa.success/failure with reason codes.
[23:00] Jordan: Any limitations on retention for extremely large customers? If we generate petabytes of logs do you have a cap?
[23:08] Miguel: We accommodate large volumes but we'd recommend a dedicated export/archival strategy; we'll model cost and throughput during procurement.
[23:18] Ken: Can you preserve chronological order across partitions in exported manifests?
[23:25] Priya: Manifests include global ordering metadata and export manifests can be produced with sequence numbers to preserve order across partitions.
[23:36] Alex: Alright, we're ~halfway. Any red-team or pen-test related logging specifics?
[23:44] Rosa: We run regular red-team tests and want those flagged so they don't trigger alerts. Can we tag test events?
[23:52] Priya: You can add metadata tags to requests or run via a test principal and we'll tag events accordingly; we also support test-mode that suppresses alerting.
[24:05] Jordan: Are admin events immutable once exported? We saw earlier WORM options but just double-check.
[24:12] Miguel: If you export to a WORM-enabled bucket then yes, within the retention window. Otherwise normal lifecycle applies.
[24:22] Rosa: How does your audit schema handle bulk operations, like a policy change that affects thousands of models?
[24:31] Priya: Bulk operations create a bulk.operation event and then we batch sub-events; the manifest links them together so auditors can see the batch and each effected resource.
[24:45] Ken: A compliance nuance — can you tag events with regulatory classification (e.g., PHI, PII) at ingestion time?
[24:55] Priya: We have an enrichment pipeline that can tag events. For hosted default we tag PII/PHI if detection is enabled; for Dedicated we recommend running your detectors and injecting classification at the forwarder.
[25:10] Jordan: Ok, let's talk about the practical next steps and timing. We'll need the artifacts for our legal review and then schedule a shorter follow-up in two weeks.
[25:22] Alex: Sounds good. We'll aim to deliver the artifacts in 48-72 hours.
[25:28] Priya: I'll drop the audit-schema CSV and Splunk query repo link in the notes; Miguel will include the demo recording.
[25:36] [people typing sounds]
[25:40] Alex: Any final quick questions?
[25:45] Rosa: One — if we go Dedicated, how does Redwood ensure operator access is logged and approved? You mentioned an approver workflow?
[25:54] Miguel: We have an operator access flow where operator actions require ephemeral credentials and an approver step; those actions are logged to an operator-audit log which can be exported.
[26:10] Jordan: Could you also indicate the CNIs involved? Some of our networking folks asked about CNI plugins — sorry, that might be too deep.
[26:18] Priya: We can spin a deep-dive with infra folks; not necessary for today's call.
[26:25] Alex: Ok let's recap verbally and then we'll post precise next steps.
[26:30] Alex: Recap: Redwood will provide hosted-default logging one-pager, audit-schema CSV, Splunk/SIEM query templates, demo recording, pricing for extended retention, and a legal addendum draft for CMK/exports. NovaHealth to confirm required retention windows and provide list of admin events to focus on. We'll reconvene week of 2025-07-28.
[26:55] Ken: Sounds good.
[26:58] Jordan: Thanks everyone.
[27:02] Alex: Thanks — we'll follow up.
[27:10] [END OF MAIN Q&A — remaining time spent on side clarifications and recording wrap]
[27:20] [28:00] Miguel: One quick note in chat — sample schema link is in the meeting notes, and the Splunk repo is at github.com/redwood-infra/splunk-templates (sample)
[29:00] Rosa: I'll email our retention matrix after this call.
[31:15] Alex: We'll capture action items in CRM and push docs to the shared drive.
[33:05] [small cross-talk; people say thanks]
[35:00] Alex: Okay wrapping up — I'll drop the one-pager and hosted default note in the follow-up email.
[37:00] Jordan: Appreciate it.
[39:00] [call ends; recording stops]
